The test image shows a corn stalk split open with completely shredded pith, leaving only fibrous tan/brown vascular strands — classic internal stalk rot presentation.

**Key visual observations:**
- Stalk opened longitudinally showing internal tissue
- Pith has fully disintegrated, leaving only stringy vascular bundles
- Tan/brown color throughout, fibrous/shredded texture
- Placed on dark blue/black background

**Comparison with reference:** The Charcoal_stalk_rot reference collage (bottom-right panel especially) is nearly identical — same dark background, same tan-brown shredded vascular strands with fully decomposed pith. This matches the description of "shredded stalks with only stringy vascular strands remaining" and "pith tissue disintegrates leaving vascular tissue with a granular, gray appearance."

The appearance is distinct from Diplodia (which would show white mold or black pycnidia), Anthracnose (shiny black rind discoloration), or Fusarium (pink/red internal discoloration).
